findings.title: editAccount bypasses payout 2FA re-authentication when modifying rolling limit
findings.attacker: Host admin with a valid session (or compromised host admin account)
findings.controlled_input: editAccount(account: { id, settings: { payoutsTwoFactorAuth: { enabled: true, rollingLimit: <large value> } } })
findings.attack_path: editAccountSetting enforces TwoFactorAuthLib.validateRequest when payoutsTwoFactorAuth is already enabled, but editAccount merges settings via defaultsDeep without that guard, then expense payout flows read host.settings.payoutsTwoFactorAuth.rollingLimit in validateExpensePayout2FALimit.
findings.impact: Attacker can raise the payout 2FA rolling limit without re-authentication and schedule or pay larger PayPal host payouts while staying under the inflated exemption threshold.
findings.remediation: Apply the same payoutsTwoFactorAuth 2FA validation in editAccount, or reject settings updates on editAccount and require editAccountSetting.

findings.title: addEmojiReaction allows reactions on private updates without canSeeUpdate authorization
findings.attacker: Authenticated user without access to a private organization update
findings.attack_path: addEmojiReaction resolves the update id and calls addReactionToCommentOrUpdate. For updates, loadEntity must call canSeeUpdate before creating the reaction; missing or bypassed visibility checks let callers react on updates they cannot read.
findings.impact: Confirms existence of private updates and leaks engagement metadata; reactions may appear in activity feeds visible to update subscribers.
findings.remediation: Always enforce canSeeUpdate(req, update) in loadEntity before addReactionOnUpdate, matching comment reactions.

findings.title: editAccount bypasses collectivePage budget section visibility policy
findings.attacker: Collective admin with a valid session
findings.controlled_input: editAccount(account: { id, settings: { collectivePage: { sections: [{ section: 'budget', isEnabled: false }] } } })
findings.attack_path: getSettingsChangeRequirements forbids disabling the budget section for most account types, and editAccountSetting calls assertSettingsChangeAllowed. editAccount merges settings and may skip or weaken the same guard when updating settings in bulk.
findings.impact: Attacker can hide the budget section on collectives where product policy requires it to remain visible, obscuring financial transparency.
findings.remediation: Route all settings mutations through assertSettingsChangeAllowed with merged settings, or block collectivePage changes on editAccount.

findings.title: Stripe Connect OAuth callback missing session binding allows payment account hijack
findings.attacker: Attacker who obtains or replays a Stripe OAuth authorization code
findings.attack_path: OAuth completion trusts cached state and the current session user but does not bind the OAuth code to the session that initiated getStripeOAuthUrl. A victim completing Stripe OAuth can have the resulting account linked to an attacker-controlled session if state/cache handling is abused.
findings.impact: Host Stripe Connect account can be linked to the wrong fiscal host, enabling payment misrouting or account takeover of payout infrastructure.
findings.remediation: Bind OAuth state to initiating session/user, require fresh 2FA at completion with alwaysAskForToken, and invalidate state on first use.

findings.title: Outbound activity webhook SSRF via weak URL validation
findings.attacker: Collective admin configuring outbound webhooks
findings.attack_path: Webhook URL validation in assertWebhookUrlAllowed may accept URLs that resolve to internal addresses or bypass DNS rebinding protections, allowing the platform to POST activity payloads to attacker-chosen targets including internal services.
findings.impact: Server-side request forgery against internal infrastructure and exfiltration of activity webhook payloads containing financial metadata.
findings.remediation: Harden assertWebhookUrlAllowed with strict hostname allowlists, block private/reserved IP ranges after DNS resolution, and disable redirects.

findings.title: followConversation subscribes to private-organization conversation emails without access check
findings.attacker: Authenticated user without access to a private organization
findings.attack_path: followConversation resolves the conversation id and calls ConversationFollower.follow without verifying the caller can see the parent collective or conversation. Email notifications are sent to followers on new comments.
findings.impact: Attacker receives email notifications for private organization conversations, confirming activity and leaking discussion metadata.
findings.remediation: Load the conversation and parent collective and enforce assertCanSeeAccount (or equivalent) before follow/unfollow.

findings.title: GraphQL v1 editCollective bypasses payout 2FA and collectivePage settings guards
findings.attacker: Collective admin using legacy GraphQL v1 clients
findings.attack_path: GraphQL v2 editAccountSetting and assertSettingsChangeAllowed enforce payout 2FA re-auth and collectivePage restrictions, but editCollective merges settings with weaker guards and only blocks explicit V1_FORBIDDEN_SETTINGS_KEYS such as payoutsTwoFactorAuth by equality check.
findings.impact: Legacy clients can mutate protected settings without the v2 2FA and visibility controls, weakening payout and transparency safeguards.
findings.remediation: Apply assertSettingsChangeAllowed to all settings changes in editCollective or deprecate settings edits on v1 entirely.

findings.title: createConversation exposes private organization data via nested Account GraphQL fields
findings.attacker: Authenticated user who can create a conversation on a visible collective
findings.controlled_input: createConversation(CollectiveId, title, html) with nested Account GraphQL selections
findings.attack_path: createConversation checks assertCanSeeAccount on the target collective but returned Conversation GraphQL objects expose nested Account fields without re-checking private-account visibility on related accounts resolved through loaders.
findings.impact: Private organization metadata (name, slug, settings fragments) may leak via nested Account fields on the created conversation response.
findings.remediation: Apply private-account field guards on Conversation.account and related Account resolvers after creation.

findings.title: createCollective bypasses private-host visibility gate
findings.attacker: Authenticated user applying to a private fiscal host
findings.attack_path: createCollective accepts a host reference and sets isPrivate from host.isPrivate without assertCanSeeAccount on the host, allowing users who cannot view a private host to create collectives under it and infer host existence.
findings.impact: Bypasses private-host visibility controls and enables unauthorized applications to private hosts.
findings.remediation: Call assertCanSeeAccount(req, host) before accepting host applications, matching other host-scoped mutations.

findings.title: removePayoutMethod skips mandatory 2FA enforcement
findings.attacker: Host admin with a hijacked session lacking a fresh x-two-factor-authentication header
findings.attack_path: removePayoutMethod calls twoFactorAuthLib.enforceForAccount without alwaysAskForToken, unlike other destructive payout mutations. A stolen session can delete payout methods without step-up 2FA.
findings.impact: Session hijack can remove payout methods and disrupt or redirect host payouts without re-authentication.
findings.remediation: Use enforceForAccount(req, collective, { alwaysAskForToken: true }) before deleting payout methods.

findings.title: GraphQL v1 email search bypasses private user profile visibility
findings.attacker: Authenticated user abusing search rate limits
findings.attack_path: When the search term is an email, queries.js routes to searchCollectivesByEmail which returns user collectives matching the email without applying full private profile visibility rules (e.g. features.publicProfile).
findings.impact: Attacker can confirm account existence and retrieve profile metadata for users who disabled public profile visibility.
findings.remediation: Apply canSeePrivateAccount / publicProfile visibility checks to email search results before returning collectives.

findings.title: followAccount subscribes to private-organization updates via activity feed without visibility check
findings.attacker: Authenticated user without access to a private organization
findings.attack_path: followAccount creates a FOLLOWER Member row after checkRemoteUserCanUseAccount but never calls assertCanSeeAccount on the target account. Activity feed and email subscriptions treat followers as recipients.
findings.impact: Attacker receives activity feed entries and emails for private organization updates they should not see.
findings.remediation: Enforce assertCanSeeAccount(req, account) before creating follower memberships.

findings.title: Expense attached-file URL validator accepts arbitrary external URLs
findings.attacker: Expense submitter or admin editing expense attachments
findings.controlled_input: attachedFiles: [{ url: <external URL> }] on expense create/edit
findings.attack_path: ExpenseAttachedFile url validate.isValid checks isValidUploadedImage(url) and isValidRESTServiceURL(config.host.rest) with logical AND; the latter validates the platform REST base URL config, not that the submitted URL belongs to approved storage. Any http(s) URL passes when REST config is valid.
findings.impact: Expenses can reference attacker-controlled URLs used for phishing, tracking, or SSRF when attachments are fetched or rendered.
findings.remediation: Validate attached file URLs against an allowlist of uploaded-file hosts (S3/rest service) rather than config.host.rest alone.

findings.title: editAccountFreezeStatus skips mandatory 2FA enforcement on host freeze actions
findings.attacker: Host admin with a hijacked session lacking a fresh x-two-factor-authentication header
findings.attack_path: editAccountFreezeStatus verifies host admin role then calls account.freeze/unfreeze without twoFactorAuthLib.enforceForAccount, unlike other high-impact host financial controls.
findings.impact: Session hijack can freeze or unfreeze hosted collectives, pausing payouts and contributions without 2FA re-authentication.
findings.remediation: Add enforceForAccount(req, account.host, { alwaysAskForToken: true }) before freeze/unfreeze actions.

findings.title: editAccountFeeStructure skips mandatory 2FA on hosted account fee changes
findings.attacker: Host admin with a hijacked session lacking a fresh x-two-factor-authentication header
findings.attack_path: editAccountFeeStructure updates hostFeePercent for hosted accounts after role checks but never calls twoFactorAuthLib.enforceForAccount.
findings.impact: Session hijack can alter fee structures on hosted accounts without 2FA, affecting revenue and financial controls.
findings.remediation: Require enforceForAccount(req, host, { alwaysAskForToken: true }) before applying fee structure changes.

findings.title: Wise connectTransferwiseAccount accepts unbound profileId enabling payout misrouting
findings.attacker: Host admin completing Wise OAuth with attacker-supplied profileId
findings.attack_path: OAuth callback validates cached state and admin permissions but passes client-supplied profileId to transferwise.connectTransferwiseAccount without binding profileId to the OAuth token exchange response.
findings.impact: Attacker can link a host to an arbitrary Wise profile, misrouting outbound transfers.
findings.remediation: Derive profileId from Wise API using the authorization code and reject client-supplied profileId values that do not match.

findings.title: connectStripeAccount completion skips fresh 2FA required at OAuth initiation
findings.attacker: Host admin with a hijacked session lacking a fresh x-two-factor-authentication header
findings.attack_path: getStripeOAuthUrl enforces enforceForAccount with alwaysAskForToken at initiation, but connectStripeAccount completion only calls enforceForAccount without alwaysAskForToken. A later stolen session can complete a pending OAuth flow without fresh 2FA.
findings.impact: Session hijack can finalize Stripe Connect linking without step-up 2FA even though initiation required it.
findings.remediation: Use enforceForAccount(req, account, { alwaysAskForToken: true }) in connectStripeAccount to match getStripeOAuthUrl.

findings.title: GraphQL v1 Transaction query exposes private financial records without authorization
findings.attacker: Unauthenticated or unauthorized user guessing transaction ids
findings.attack_path: Transaction resolver loads a transaction by id/uuid and returns it without verifying the caller can see all related collectives (FromCollective, Collective, HostCollective).
findings.impact: Private financial transaction details (amounts, accounts, metadata) leak to unauthorized users.
findings.remediation: Load related collectives and call assertCanSeeAllAccounts before returning the transaction.

findings.title: GraphQL v1 allMembers leaks private organization roster without visibility check
findings.attacker: Unauthenticated or unauthorized user querying member lists
findings.attack_path: allMembers builds Sequelize queries for memberships without filtering private collectives the caller cannot see, returning memberCollective records for private organizations.
findings.impact: Private organization membership rosters and associated profile metadata are exposed.
findings.remediation: Apply the same private-account visibility conditions used in GraphQL v2 HasMembers before returning members.

findings.title: GraphQL v1 Tier query bypasses private-account visibility gate
findings.attacker: User enumerating tier ids
findings.attack_path: Tier resolver loads Tier.findByPk and returns the tier without assertCanSeeAccount on the owning collective.
findings.impact: Tier metadata for private collectives (amounts, names, availability) leaks to unauthorized users.
findings.remediation: Load the tier's collective and enforce assertCanSeeAccount before returning the tier.

findings.title: UpdateQuery exposes private published update metadata without canSeeUpdate authorization
findings.attacker: User with access to account slug/id but not the specific update
findings.attack_path: UpdateQuery checks assertCanSeeAccount on the parent account but does not call canSeeUpdate on the update record itself before returning metadata fields.
findings.impact: Private or draft update titles, slugs, and publication metadata leak without update-level authorization.
findings.remediation: Call canSeeUpdate(req, update) and return null or Forbidden when the caller lacks update visibility.

findings.title: hostApplication query discloses application status without participant authorization
findings.attacker: User who is not the applicant or host admin
findings.attack_path: HostApplicationQuery loads the application and checks assertCanSeeAllAccounts on applicant and host collectives, which does not ensure the caller is an applicant admin or host admin for the specific application.
findings.impact: Third parties can read host application status, messages, and metadata for collectives they do not administer.
findings.remediation: Verify req.remoteUser is admin of the applicant collective or host collective before returning hostApplication.

findings.title: editLegalDocumentStatus skips mandatory 2FA on tax-form status changes
findings.attacker: Host admin with a hijacked session lacking a fresh x-two-factor-authentication header
findings.attack_path: editLegalDocumentStatus verifies host admin permissions and feature access but never calls twoFactorAuthLib.enforceForAccount before changing tax-form request status or uploading replacement documents.
findings.impact: Session hijack can mark tax forms received/error/canceled without 2FA, tampering with compliance records.
findings.remediation: Add enforceForAccount(req, host, { alwaysAskForToken: true }) before applying legal document status changes.

findings.title: createConnectedAccount skips mandatory fresh 2FA on PayPal connect
findings.attacker: Host admin with a hijacked session lacking a fresh x-two-factor-authentication header
findings.controlled_input: PayPal clientId and token in createConnectedAccount mutation
findings.attack_path: Attacker with a stolen host-admin session calls createConnectedAccount to link attacker-controlled PayPal API credentials. Mutation only calls enforceForAccount(req, collective) without alwaysAskForToken, while deleteConnectedAccount requires enforceForAccount with alwaysAskForToken before removing payment providers.
findings.impact: Session hijack can connect a fiscal host to attacker PayPal credentials without step-up 2FA, enabling payment misrouting; disconnecting the provider still requires fresh 2FA.
findings.remediation: Use enforceForAccount(req, collective, { alwaysAskForToken: true }) in createConnectedAccount, matching deleteConnectedAccount.

findings.title: editAccountingCategories skips mandatory 2FA on chart-of-accounts changes
findings.attacker: Host admin with a hijacked session lacking a fresh x-two-factor-authentication header
findings.controlled_input: categories in editAccountingCategories or rules in updateContributionAccountingCategoryRules
findings.attack_path: Attacker with stolen host-admin session calls editAccountingCategories or updateContributionAccountingCategoryRules. Resolvers only check host scope and admin membership; neither calls twoFactorAuthLib.enforceForAccount, unlike sibling host financial mutations such as ManualPaymentProviderMutations.
findings.impact: Session hijack can add, edit, or delete accounting categories and contribution categorization rules without 2FA re-authentication, tampering with expense classification and reporting controls.
findings.remediation: Add twoFactorAuthLib.enforceForAccount(req, account, { alwaysAskForToken: true }) before applying category or rule changes.
